key_insight: Flow-dependent LES filter widths can pass floating-point perturbations through the SGS model with little attenuation, so numerical noise can become physically relevant on heterogeneous hardware.
engineering_relevance: A robust max-min compressed, velocity-gradient-bounded filter-width formulation can reduce architecture-induced sensitivity while preserving flow dependence in LES.
method: Analyze how LSQ-based filter width transmits perturbations from mesh metrics
Introduce scalar max-min compression of directional mesh scales
Add bounded modulation from the resolved velocity gradient to reroute perturbations
evidence_signal: The approach is evaluated on CPU and GPU for cylinder flow at Re=3900 and Taylor-Green vortex at Re=1600, showing strong transmission effects in the former and no comparable macroscopic response on orthogonal grids in the latter.
watch_item: The mitigation depends on mesh geometry and flow coupling, so gains may be limited or absent in configurations where the perturbation pathway is structurally weak.
paper_title: On the transmission of floating-point perturbations in flow-dependent filter-width formulations in Large-Eddy Simulation
